title: My whole body aches
goal: On campus, tell Sēf about your first week at the gym and why everything aches, and take his advice
tip: ṣār + a present verb says what you've started doing: ṣirt arūḥ in-nādi 'I've started going to the gym'. A body part with yʿawwir 'hurts' takes the person as the object: jismi killah yʿawwirni 'my whole body aches' (jism is masculine, so y-).
grammar: recycle: ṣār + present verb for a new habit (ṣirt arūḥ)
dialogue: A
شفيك تمشي جي؟ لا تقول طحت!
shfīk timshi chī? la tgūl ṭiḥt!
What's up with the way you're walking? Don't tell me you fell!
B
لا، صرت أروح النادي. جسمي كله يعورني
la, ṣirt arūḥ in-nādi. jismi killah yʿawwirni
No, I've started going to the gym. My whole body aches.
A
عادي، أول أسبوع العضلات كلها تعورك. شو سويت؟
ʿādi, awwal usbūʿ il-ʿaẓalāt killha tʿawwrak. shu sawwēt?
That's normal: in the first week all your muscles ache. What did you do?
B
لعبت حديد ساعة كاملة، وثاني يوم ركضت
liʿabt ḥadīd sāʿa kāmla, w thāni yōm rakaẓt
I lifted weights for a whole hour, and the next day I went running.
A
ساعة كاملة من أول مرة؟ منو قال لك تسوي جي؟
sāʿa kāmla min awwal marra? minu gāl-lak tsawwi chī?
A whole hour, the first time? Who told you to do that?
B
المدرب. يقول ثلاث مرات في الأسبوع
il-mudarrib. ygūl thalāth marrāt fi l-usbūʿ
The trainer. He says three times a week.
A
زين، بس على هونك. جسمك ما تعود للحين، يباله وقت
zēn, bas ʿala hōnak. jismak ma tʿawwad lil-ḥīn, yabā-lah wagt
Fine, but take it easy. Your body isn't used to it yet; it needs time.
B
معك حق. وانت؟ تلعب حديد؟
maʿak ḥagg. w inta? tilʿab ḥadīd?
You're right. And you? Do you lift weights?
A
هيه، من سنتين. تبي تيي وياي باكر؟
hē, min santēn. tabi tiyi wiyyāy bāchir?
Yes, for two years. Do you want to come with me tomorrow?
B
إن شاء الله، بس بعد العصر. الصبح ما أقدر أقوم
in shāʼ allāh, bas baʿd il-ʿaṣir. iṣ-ṣubḥ ma agdar agūm
God willing, but after ʿaṣr. In the morning I can't get up.
items: I've started going to the gym
you'll also hear il-jīm (الجيم); nādi is also a sports club
my whole body aches, I ache all over
I lifted weights; you lifted weights (to a man)
lit. I played iron; to a woman: liʿabti ḥadīd; he lifts weights: yilʿab ḥadīd
the next day, the day after

title: I'm on a diet
goal: At a team lunch in the office, Maryam offers everyone sweets; say you're on a diet and what you've cut down on
tip: ma ʿād + a present verb says 'not any more': ma ʿidt ākil ḥalawiyyāt 'I don't eat sweets any more'. It takes the person: ma ʿidt (I), ma ʿād (he). With a participle, the ending shows who: ana msawwi rijīm 'I'm on a diet' (a woman: msawwya).
grammar: recycle: ma ʿād + present verb, 'not any more'
dialogue: A
تفضلوا، يايبة لكم حلويات من البيت. خذ يا سالم، لا تستحي
tfaẓẓalu, yāyba-lkum ḥalawiyyāt min il-bēt. khudh yā Sālim, la tistiḥi
Help yourselves, I've brought you all sweets from home. Take one, Sālim, don't be shy.
B
ما أقدر، أنا مسوي رجيم
ma agdar, ana msawwi rijīm
I can't, I'm on a diet.
A
رجيم؟ انت؟ بس انت ضعفت، باين عليك!
rijīm? inta? bas inta ẓiʿaft, bāyin ʿalēk!
A diet? You? But you've lost weight, it shows!
B
صج؟ زاد وزني لما صرت أسوق لكل مكان
ṣij? zād wazni lamma ṣirt asūg l-kill makān
Really? I put on weight when I started driving everywhere.
A
وشو غيرت؟
w shu ghayyart?
And what have you changed?
B
ما عدت آكل حلويات، وخففت السكر
ma ʿidt ākil ḥalawiyyāt, w khaffaft is-sukkar
I don't eat sweets any more, and I've cut down on sugar.
A
ما شاء الله عليك! أنا ما أقدر أقاوم الحلو، خصوصا ويا القهوة
mā shāʼ allāh ʿalēk! ana ma agdar agāwim il-ḥilu, khuṣūṣan wiyya l-gahwa
Good for you! I can't resist sweet things, especially with coffee.
B
ولا أنا! بس أحاول. شوي عيش ووايد سلطة
wala ana! bas aḥāwil. shwayy ʿēsh w wāyid salaṭa
Nor can I! But I'm trying. A bit of rice and lots of salad.
A
عيل خذ وحدة بس، وحدة ما تضر
ʿayal khudh waḥda bas, waḥda ma tẓurr
Then take just one; one won't hurt.
B
زين، وحدة بس. بس لا تقولين للمدرب!
zēn, waḥda bas. bas la tgūlīn lil-mudarrib!
OK, just one. But don't tell my trainer!
items: you've lost weight (to a man); I've lost weight
to a woman: ẓiʿafti; in the Gulf ẓiʿīf usually means thin
it shows, you can tell (lit. it's visible on you) (to a man)
I've put on weight (lit. my weight went up)
I've cut down on sugar; you've cut down on sugar (to a man)
to a woman: khaffafti is-sukkar; sukkar 'sugar' is spelled like sakkar 'he closed'
I've brought you (said by a woman, to a group)

title: I haven't slept properly for a week
goal: At a karak stand, tell Sēf you can't sleep, and hear what changed things for him
tip: ṣār-li + a time + a present verb says how long something has been going on: ṣār-li usbūʿ ma anām ʿadil 'I haven't slept properly for a week'. ṣirt + a present verb is the change: ṣirt anām aḥsan 'I've started sleeping better'.
grammar: recycle: ṣār-li + time for 'for (a week) now'
dialogue: A
شكلك تعبان. بعدك ما تنام زين؟
shaklak taʿbān. baʿdak ma tnām zēn?
You look tired. Still not sleeping well?
B
لا والله. صار لي أسبوع ما أنام عدل
la wallāh. ṣār-li usbūʿ ma anām ʿadil
No, honestly. I haven't slept properly for a week.
A
ليش؟ تفكر في شي؟
lēsh? tfakkir fi shay?
Why? Is something on your mind?
B
لا، بس أنام الساعة وحدة، وأتقلب لين الفجر
la, bas anām is-sāʿa waḥda, w atgallab lēn il-fajr
No, I just go to bed at one and toss and turn till dawn.
A
وقبل لا تنام؟ أكيد على التلفون
w gabil la tnām? akīd ʿala t-tilifōn
And before you sleep? On your phone, I bet.
B
هيه، أظل على التلفون ساعة وأكثر
hē, aẓall ʿala t-tilifōn sāʿa w akthar
Yes, I stay on my phone for an hour or more.
A
أنا كنت جي. لما خليت التلفون برا الغرفة، صرت أنام أحسن
ana kint chī. lamma khallēt it-tilifōn barra l-ghurfa, ṣirt anām aḥsan
I used to be like that. When I left my phone outside the room, I started sleeping better.
B
زين، بجرب. بس الغفوة بعد الغدا ما أقدر أخليها!
zēn, bajarrib. bas il-ghafwa baʿd il-ghada ma agdar akhallīha!
OK, I'll try. But I can't give up my nap after lunch!
A
لا تخليها، بس خلها قصيرة. وأنا ما أشرب قهوة بعد العصر، تطير النوم
la tkhallīha, bas khallha gaṣīra. w ana ma ashrab gahwa baʿd il-ʿaṣir, tṭayyir in-nōm
Don't give it up, just keep it short. And I don't drink coffee after ʿaṣr; it keeps me awake.
items: for a week now, it's been a week (for me)
I stay on my phone, I keep scrolling on my phone
outside the room, out of the room
I've started sleeping better, I sleep better now
keep it short (a feminine thing) (to a man)
it (f.) keeps you awake (lit. it makes sleep fly off)

title: One thing at a time
goal: At the office, Maryam notices you're stressed about two reports; say what's getting to you and take her advice
tip: Advice is mostly commands and la + a present verb: khudhhum wāḥid wāḥid 'take them one at a time', khudh brēk 'take a break', la tḥuṭṭ fi bālak 'don't let it get to you'. To a woman they end in -i / -īn: khudhi brēk, la tḥuṭṭīn fi bālich.
grammar: recycle: commands and la + present verb for advice
dialogue: A
سالم، من الصبح وانت ساكت. شفيك؟
Sālim, min iṣ-ṣubḥ w inta sākit. shfīk?
Sālim, you've been quiet since this morning. What's wrong?
B
متوتر شوي. عندي تقريرين لازم أسلّمهم الخميس
mitwattir shwayy. ʿindi taqrīrēn lāzim asallimhum il-khamīs
I'm a bit stressed. I've got two reports to hand in on Thursday.
A
بس الخميس بعيد! ليش متوتر جي؟
bas il-khamīs baʿīd! lēsh mitwattir chī?
But Thursday's ages away! Why are you so stressed?
B
المدير يبيهم مرتبين، وأنا مضغوط من كل صوب
il-mudīr yabīhum mrattabīn, w ana maẓghūṭ min kill ṣōb
The manager wants them done properly, and I'm under pressure from every side.
A
هد أعصابك. خذهم واحد واحد: الأول باكر، والثاني الأربعا
hidd aʿṣābak. khudhhum wāḥid wāḥid: il-awwal bāchir, w ith-thāni l-arbaʿa
Calm down. Take them one at a time: the first one tomorrow, the second on Wednesday.
B
معج حق. بس ما أنام زين من الضغط
maʿich ḥagg. bas ma anām zēn min iẓ-ẓaghiṭ
You're right. But I can't sleep well with the stress.
A
لا تحط في بالك وايد. الشغل ما يخلص، كل يوم في شي يديد
la tḥuṭṭ fi bālak wāyid. ish-shughul ma yikhlaṣ, kill yōm fī shay yidīd
Don't let it get to you so much. Work never ends; there's something new every day.
B
صدقتي. يمكن أحتاج بريك
ṣidagti. yimkin aḥtāj brēk
True. Maybe I need a break.
A
هيه، خذ بريك. اطلع تمشى عشر دقايق ورد
hē, khudh brēk. iṭlaʿ itmashsha ʿashr dagāyig w rudd
Yes, take a break. Go out for a ten-minute walk and come back.
B
فكرة حلوة. بطلع أتمشى شوي، وبرد أكمل
fikra ḥilwa. baṭlaʿ atmashsha shwayy, w barudd akammil
Good idea. I'll go out for a little walk and come back to finish.
items: and you've been quiet, with you (sitting there) saying nothing (to a man)
to a woman: w inti sākta; (recognise)
from every side, from all directions
don't let it get to you, don't dwell on it (to a man)
to a woman: la tḥuṭṭīn fi bālich
work never ends (lit. work doesn't finish)
to a woman: khudhi brēk; also istirāḥa (استراحة) 'a break'
I go for a walk, I take a stroll
go for a walk (to a man): itmashsha

title: Karak, step by step
goal: At your flat in Mirdif, Sēf shows you how to make karak; follow each step, ask about amounts, and say the recipe back
tip: Explain a process with commands and order words: awwal shay 'first', baʿdēn 'then', lēn 'until'. khallah + a present verb is 'let it …': khallah yighli 'let it boil'. To check you've got it, say the steps back and end with ṣaḥḥ?
grammar: recycle: commands with awwal shay, baʿdēn, lēn for steps
dialogue: B
أبي أتعلم أسوي كرك مثل اللي عند المحل
abi atʿallam asawwi karak mithil illi ʿind il-maḥall
I want to learn to make karak like the one at the shop.
A
سهلة! أول شي، حط الماي على النار، وحط فيه شاي وهيل
sahla! awwal shay, ḥuṭṭ il-māy ʿala n-nār, w ḥuṭṭ fīh chāy w hēl
Easy! First, put the water on the heat, and put tea and cardamom in it.
B
كم ملعقة شاي؟
cham milʿagat chāy?
How many spoons of tea?
A
ملعقة لكل كوب، أو أكثر إذا تبيه ثقيل. وخله يغلي
milʿaga l-kill kūb, aw akthar idha tabīh thagīl. w khallah yighli
A spoon for each cup, or more if you want it strong. And let it boil.
B
وبعدين؟ الحليب؟
w baʿdēn? il-ḥalīb?
And then? The milk?
A
هيه، حط الحليب والسكر، وخله على نار هادية
hē, ḥuṭṭ il-ḥalīb w is-sukkar, w khallah ʿala nār hādya
Yes, add the milk and sugar, and leave it on a low heat.
B
لين متى؟
lēn mita?
Until when?
A
لين يفور مرتين. بس انتبه، لا تخليه يطلع برا القدر
lēn yifūr marratēn. bas intibih, la tkhallīh yiṭlaʿ barra l-jidir
Until it froths up twice. But careful, don't let it boil over (lit. go out of the pot).
B
يعني: الماي والشاي والهيل، بعدين الحليب والسكر، ويفور مرتين. صح؟
yaʿni: il-māy w ich-chāy w il-hēl, baʿdēn il-ḥalīb w is-sukkar, w yifūr marratēn. ṣaḥḥ?
So: water, tea and cardamom, then milk and sugar, and it froths up twice. Right?
A
بالضبط! وفي ناس يحطون زعفران بعد، على كيفك
biẓ-ẓabṭ! w fī nās yḥuṭṭūn zaʿfarān baʿad, ʿala kēfak
Exactly! And some people add saffron too; up to you.
items: put the water on (to heat) (to a man)
to a woman: ḥuṭṭi il-māy ʿala n-nār
a spoon of tea: milʿagat chāy
until it froths up, until it boils up
task: This week: search YouTube for «طريقة الكرك» (how to make karak) or «طبخ إماراتي» (Emirati cooking). Watch one recipe and note three steps the cook gives (listen for حط, خله and لين). Then explain the recipe aloud, step by step, in under a minute. Within a minute you should hear شو / مب (UAE) or شنو / مو (Kuwait); if you hear سوف, ليس or هل all the time, it's fuṣḥā: pick another clip.

title: It counts your steps
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Sēf there, show him how to use a step-counter app on his phone, one step at a time
tip: kill ma + a present verb is 'every time, whenever': kill ma timshi, yiḥsib 'every time you walk, it counts'. Explaining to an elder, keep each step short and add yā ʿammi or ṭāl ʿumrak; the verbs are still the ordinary 'you' forms: tiftaḥah, tḥuṭṭah.
grammar: recycle: kill ma + present verb, 'every time'
dialogue: A
يا ولدي، الدكتور يقول لي أمشي أكثر. بس كيف أعرف كم مشيت؟
yā wildi, id-daktōr ygūl-li amshi akthar. bas chēf aʿarf cham mishēt?
Son, the doctor tells me to walk more. But how do I know how far I've walked?
B
سهلة يا عمي. في تطبيق يحسب خطواتك
sahla yā ʿammi. fī taṭbīg yiḥsib khaṭawātak
That's easy, uncle. There's an app that counts your steps.
A
تطبيق؟ أنا ما أدري عن هالأشيا. علمني شوي شوي
taṭbīg? ana ma adri ʿan hal-ashya. ʿallimni shwayy shwayy
An app? I don't know about these things. Teach me slowly.
B
عطني تلفونك، طال عمرك. أول شي ننزل التطبيق
ʿaṭni tilifōnak, ṭāl ʿumrak. awwal shay nnazzil it-taṭbīg
Give me your phone, sir. First we download the app.
A
تفضل. وبعدين؟
tfaẓẓal. w baʿdēn?
Here you are. And then?
B
بعدين تحطه في جيبك. كل ما تمشي، يحسب
baʿdēn tḥuṭṭah fi jēbak. kill ma timshi, yiḥsib
Then you put it in your pocket. Every time you walk, it counts.
A
بروحه؟ ما أضغط شي؟
b-rūḥah? ma aẓghaṭ shay?
By itself? I don't press anything?
B
لا، بروحه. وفي الليل شوف هني، يطلع لك كم خطوة مشيت
la, b-rūḥah. w fi l-lēl shūf hni, yiṭlaʿ-lak cham khaṭwa mishēt
No, by itself. And at night look here: it shows you how many steps you've walked.
A
ما شاء الله! والله زمانكم غير يا ولدي. الله يحفظك
mā shāʼ allāh! wallāh zamānkum ghēr yā wildi. allāh yiḥfaẓak
Wonderful! Your times really are different, son. God keep you.
B
الله يحفظك يا عمي. وأنا حاضر
allāh yiḥfaẓak yā ʿammi. w ana ḥāẓir
God keep you, uncle. And I'm always here to help.
items: it counts your steps (to a man)
we download the app; let's download the app
every time you walk, whenever you walk (to a man)
to a woman: kill ma timshīn
it shows you, it comes up for you (on a screen) (to a man)
I don't know about these things
لا أعرف شيئًا عن هذه الأشياء
your times are different, it's a different world now (to a group)

title: Stuck in the sand
goal: At a café, tell Fahad the long story of how you and Sēf got stuck in the sand on the way to a camp
tip: Set the scene with w + a pronoun + a participle or a present verb, 'as, while': w niḥin rāyḥīn 'as we were on our way', w ana aḥfir 'while I was digging'. Then move on with fi nuṣṣ iṭ-ṭarīg 'halfway', fajʼa, and close with min dhāk il-yōm 'since that day'.
grammar: narrative markers: w + pronoun + participle ('as …'), min dhāk il-yōm
dialogue: A
سمعت إنكم غرزتوا في البر! شنو صار؟
simaʿt innakum gharaztu fi l-barr! shinu ṣār?
I heard you got stuck in the desert! What happened?
B
لا تذكرني! ونحن رايحين المخيم، دخلنا طريق رمل
la tdhakkirni! w niḥin rāyḥīn il-mukhayyam, dakhalna ṭarīg raml
Don't remind me! As we were heading to the camp, we turned onto a sandy track.
A
بسيارتك؟
b-sayyārtak?
In your car?
B
هيه. وفي نص الطريق، غرزنا في الرمل
hē. w fi nuṣṣ iṭ-ṭarīg, gharazna fi r-raml
Yes. And halfway there, we got stuck in the sand.
A
يا ساتر! وشلون طلعتوا؟
yā sātir! w shlōn ṭlaʿtu?
Good grief! And how did you get out?
B
حاولنا ساعة كاملة. وأنا أحفر، سيف قاعد يصور!
ḥāwalna sāʿa kāmla. w ana aḥfir, Sēf gāʿid yṣawwir!
We tried for a whole hour. While I was digging, Sēf was filming!
A
هذا سيف، ما يتغير! وبعدين؟
hādha Sēf, ma yitghayyar! w baʿdēn?
That's Sēf, he never changes! And then?
B
فجأة طلع لنا شيبة بسيارة كبيرة، وسحبنا بحبل
fajʼa ṭilaʿ-lna shēba b-sayyāra kbīra, w siḥabna b-ḥabil
Suddenly an old man turned up out of nowhere in a big car and pulled us out with a rope.
A
الله يجزاه خير! أنا عمري ما غرزت، الحمد لله
allāh yjzāh khēr! ana ʿumri ma gharazt, il-ḥamdu lillāh
God reward him! I've never got stuck in my life, thank God.
B
ولا أنا قبل! ومن ذاك اليوم، ما أدخل الرمل إلا ويا سيارة ثانية
wala ana gabil! w min dhāk il-yōm, ma adkhil ir-raml illa wiyya sayyāra thānya
Nor had I, before! And since that day, I only go onto the sand with a second car.
items: as we were on our way, as we were going
halfway (there), in the middle of the journey
you got stuck (to a group): gharaztu
(he) turned up out of nowhere (lit. came out at us)
ʿumri ma shift chī 'I've never seen anything like it'
since that day, from that day on

title: I didn't know where to put myself
goal: At the office, tell Maryam and the team about the voice note you sent to the wrong group
tip: An anecdote needs a hook and a payoff: start with ṣār-li mawgif 'something happened to me', turn it with ṭilaʿ inni 'it turned out I', top it with w il-muṣība 'and the worst part', and react to your own embarrassment: ma ʿiraft wēn awaddi wiyhi.
grammar: narrative markers: ṣār-li mawgif, ṭilaʿ inn, w il-muṣība
dialogue: A
سالم، شفيك تضحك بروحك؟
Sālim, shfīk tiẓḥak b-rūḥak?
Sālim, what are you laughing at all by yourself?
B
تذكرت موقف صار لي أمس. تبون أقول لكم؟
tdhakkart mawgif ṣār-li ams. tabūn agūl-lkum?
I remembered something that happened to me yesterday. Do you want me to tell you?
A
أكيد! شو صار؟
akīd! shu ṣār?
Of course! What happened?
B
طرشت فويس لسيف، أقول المحاضرة طويلة وايد، وطلع إني طرشته لقروب الجامعة
ṭarrasht fōys l-Sēf, agūl il-muḥāẓara ṭawīla wāyid, w ṭilaʿ inni ṭarrashtah l-grūb il-jāmʿa
I sent Sēf a voice note saying the lecture was really long, and it turned out I'd sent it to the uni group.
A
لا! والدكتور في القروب؟
la! w id-daktōr fi l-grūb?
No! And is the lecturer in the group?
B
هيه! والمصيبة، رد علي: شكرا على رأيك
hē! w il-muṣība, radd ʿalay: shukran ʿala raʼyak
Yes! And the worst part: he replied to me, 'Thanks for your opinion.'
A
فشلة! وشو سويت؟
fashla! w shu sawwēt?
How embarrassing! And what did you do?
B
ما عرفت وين أودي ويهي. والكل سمعه
ma ʿiraft wēn awaddi wiyhi. w il-kill simaʿah
I didn't know where to put myself. And everyone had heard it.
A
واللي يضحك إنك قاعد تضحك عليه الحين!
w illi yiẓḥak innak gāʿid tiẓḥak ʿalēh il-ḥīn!
And the funny thing is that you're laughing about it now!
B
شو أسوي؟ اللي صار صار. بس من الحين أشوف القروب قبل لا أطرش
shu asawwi? illi ṣār ṣār. bas min il-ḥīn ashūf il-grūb gabil la aṭarrish
What can I do? What's done is done. But from now on I check the group before I send.
items: something happened to me, I had an (awkward) moment
mawgif 'a situation, an incident', not mōgif 'a parking space'
send a voice note: ṭarrish fōys
and the worst part (is), and to top it all (lit. and the disaster)
I didn't know where to put myself (lit. where to take my face)
everyone heard it (m.), everyone's heard it

title: In our day, uncle?
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Sēf there, ask him for his story about a trip to Al Ain as a young man, and keep it going respectfully
tip: An older speaker tells a story with kinna 'we were' and kān 'there was', and moves it on with il-ḥāṣil 'anyway, so'. Keep him going with short questions in the past: w shu sawwētu? w wṣaltu? and react with yā sātir! or mā shāʼ allāh.
grammar: narrative: kinna + noun, il-ḥāṣil, past-tense questions to keep a story going
dialogue: B
يا عمي، سيف يقول عندك سالفة حلوة عن العين
yā ʿammi, Sēf ygūl ʿindak sālfa ḥilwa ʿan il-ʿĒn
Uncle, Sēf says you've got a good story about Al Ain.
A
سيف ما ينسى شي! زين، اسمع. كنا شباب، ورحنا العين بسيارة قديمة
Sēf ma yinsa shay! zēn, ismaʿ. kinna shabāb, w riḥna l-ʿĒn b-sayyāra gadīma
Sēf never forgets a thing! All right, listen. We were young, and we drove to Al Ain in an old car.
B
من الشارقة؟ ووصلتوا؟
min ish-Shārja? w wṣaltu?
From Sharjah? And did you get there?
A
الحاصل، في نص الطريق خربت السيارة، والدنيا ليل، وما عندنا تلفونات
il-ḥāṣil, fi nuṣṣ iṭ-ṭarīg khirbat is-sayyāra, w id-dinya lēl, w ma ʿindana tilifōnāt
Anyway, halfway there the car broke down, it was night, and we had no phones.
B
يا ساتر! وشو سويتوا؟
yā sātir! w shu sawwētu?
Good grief! And what did you do?
A
قعدنا نتريا. وبعد ساعتين، وقف لنا ريّال ما نعرفه
gaʿadna nitrayya. w baʿd sāʿtēn, wigaf-lna rayyāl ma nʿarfah
We sat and waited. After two hours, a man we didn't know stopped for us.
B
ما شاء الله! وصلح السيارة؟
mā shāʼ allāh! w ṣallaḥ is-sayyāra?
Wonderful! And did he fix the car?
A
لا، ما قدر. بس عزمنا بيته، وبتنا عنده لين الصبح
la, ma gidar. bas ʿazamna bētah, w bitna ʿindah lēn iṣ-ṣubḥ
No, he couldn't. But he invited us to his house, and we spent the night there till morning.
B
ناس أول غير والله. سالفة ما تنتسى يا عمي
nās awwal ghēr wallāh. sālfa ma tintisa yā ʿammi
People back then really were different. That's a story you can't forget, uncle.
A
صدقت. ومن ذاك اليوم صار مثل أخوي، وللحين عياله يزوروني
ṣidagt. w min dhāk il-yōm ṣār mithil akhūy, w lil-ḥīn ʿyālah yzūrūni
True. And from that day he was like a brother to me; his children still visit me.
items: and it was dark, and night had fallen
we spent the night at his place
people in the old days, people back then
(it) can't be forgotten, unforgettable (a feminine thing)

title: The spoon in the cup
goal: At a winter desert camp, tell Sēf and the guys a clean joke, explain the punchline when he doesn't get it, and take the teasing
tip: A joke often opens with wāḥid rāḥ… 'this guy went …' and ends on a quote. If someone doesn't get it, explain it simply, in the present. Praise someone's humour with dammak khafīf 'you're funny' (lit. your blood is light).
grammar: narrative markers for a joke: wāḥid rāḥ…, gāl-lah: …
dialogue: A
يا شباب، سالم عنده نكتة. يلا، قولها!
yā shabāb, Sālim ʿindah nukta. yalla, gūlha!
Guys, Sālim's got a joke. Come on, tell it!
B
زين. واحد راح للدكتور، قال له: يا دكتور، كل ما أشرب كرك عيني تعورني
zēn. wāḥid rāḥ lid-daktōr, gāl-lah: yā daktōr, kill ma ashrab karak ʿēni tʿawwirni
OK. This guy went to the doctor and said, 'Doctor, every time I drink karak, my eye hurts.'
A
وشو قال له الدكتور؟
w shu gāl-lah id-daktōr?
And what did the doctor say to him?
B
قال له: شل الملعقة من الكوب قبل لا تشرب!
gāl-lah: shill il-milʿaga min il-kūb gabil la tishrab!
He said, 'Take the spoon out of the cup before you drink!'
A
ما فهمتها! ليش الملعقة؟
ma fhimt-ha! lēsh il-milʿaga?
I didn't get it! Why the spoon?
B
الملعقة تدخل في عينه وهو يشرب!
il-milʿaga tidkhil fi ʿēnah w huwa yishrab!
The spoon goes in his eye while he's drinking!
A
هاه، الحين فهمت. حلوة، بس قديمة!
hāh, il-ḥīn fhimt. ḥilwa, bas gadīma!
Ah, now I get it. Good one, but it's old!
B
قديمة؟ أنا أول مرة أسمعها!
gadīma? ana awwal marra asmaʿha!
Old? It's the first time I've heard it!
A
سمعتها من أبوي وأنا ياهل. دمك خفيف، بس النكتة عمرها أكبر منك!
simiʿtha min ubūy w ana yāhil. dammak khafīf, bas in-nukta ʿumrha akbar minnak!
I heard it from my dad when I was a kid. You're funny, but that joke's older than you!
B
خلاص، المرة الياية بييب لكم نكتة يديدة
khalāṣ, il-marra l-yāya bayīb-lkum nukta yidīda
Fine, next time I'll bring you all a new joke.
items: tell it, say it (a feminine thing: a joke, a story) (to a man)
this guy went, a man went (to start a joke)
take the spoon out (to a man)
to a woman: shilli il-milʿaga; shill 'take away, lift' (UAE)
while he's drinking, while he drinks
you're funny, you're good fun (lit. your blood is light) (to a man)
to a woman: dammich khafīf; the opposite: dammah thagīl 'he's tiresome'
it's older than you (a feminine thing) (to a man)
to a woman: ʿumrha akbar minnich; (recognise)
task: This week: with a tutor or exchange partner (search a tutoring site for «Emirati Arabic tutor»), tell one short, clean joke or funny story in Gulf Arabic. Open with wāḥid rāḥ… or marra min il-marrāt, use fajʼa once, and end on a quote. Ask them to tell you one back, react (dammak khafīf! or bāykha!), and ask what any word you missed means.

title: So he says
goal: At university, pass on to Sēf the story Fahad told you about nearly missing his flight, and say how far you believe it
tip: When you retell someone else's story, show it's theirs: ʿala gōlah 'according to him', ygūl-lak 'he says' (lit. he says to you), ana agūl-lak illi gāl-li 'I'm just telling you what he told me'. React with ṣij walla yitghashmar? 'is he serious or kidding?'
grammar: retelling: ʿala gōlah, ygūl-lak + past verb
dialogue: A
شفت فهد أمس؟ شو أخباره؟
shift Fahad ams? shu akhbārah?
Did you see Fahad yesterday? How's he doing?
B
هيه، وقال لي سالفة غريبة
hē, w gāl-li sālfa gharība
Yes, and he told me a strange story.
A
شو؟ قول!
shu? gūl!
What? Tell me!
B
على قوله، نام في المطار قدام البوابة، وما سمعهم ينادونه
ʿala gōlah, nām fi l-maṭār jiddām il-bawwāba, w ma simaʿhum ynādūnah
According to him, he fell asleep at the airport in front of the gate and didn't hear them calling him.
A
لا تقول! وفاتته الطيارة؟
la tgūl! w fātatah iṭ-ṭayyāra?
No way! And he missed the plane?
B
لا، هذا الحلو! يقول لك صحى، والطيارة متأخرة ساعتين
la, hādha l-ḥilu! ygūl-lak ṣiḥa, w iṭ-ṭayyāra mitʼakhkhra sāʿtēn
No, that's the best part! He says he woke up and the plane was two hours late.
A
يا حظه! بس فهد يحب يبالغ. صج ولّا يتغشمر؟
yā ḥaẓẓah! bas Fahad yḥibb ybālig. ṣij walla yitghashmar?
Lucky him! But Fahad likes to exaggerate. Is he serious or kidding?
B
ما أدري، أقول لك اللي قال لي بس
ma adri, agūl-lak illi gāl-li bas
I don't know; I'm just telling you what he told me.
A
زين، على ذمته يعني!
zēn, ʿala dhimmtah yaʿni!
OK, so that's his version, then!
B
هيه، بس أنا مصدقه. فهد ما يكذب علي
hē, bas ana mṣaddgah. Fahad ma yikdhib ʿalay
Yes, but I believe him. Fahad doesn't lie to me.
items: according to him, so he says
he missed the plane (lit. the plane passed him by)
I missed the plane: fātatni iṭ-ṭayyāra
that's the best part, that's the good bit
is he serious or (is he) kidding?
I'm telling you what he told me (to a man)
to a woman: agūl-lich illi gāl-li
so he says, that's his version (lit. on his conscience)
I believe him (said by a man)

title: Where was I?
goal: At a café, tell Fahad and Sēf how you lost the car at the mall with your parents, and keep going when Fahad keeps interrupting
tip: Hold the floor with ṭawwil bālak 'hang on', khallni akammil 'let me finish' and la tgāṭiʿni 'don't interrupt me'. Pick the thread up with wēn wiṣalt? 'where was I?', and wrap up with il-mukhtaṣar 'long story short'.
grammar: narrative markers: holding the floor and picking the story up again
dialogue: B
المهم، طلعنا من المول أنا وأمي وأبوي، وما لقينا السيارة
il-muhimm, ṭlaʿna min il-mōl ana w ummi w ubūy, w ma ligēna s-sayyāra
Anyway, my mum, my dad and I came out of the mall, and we couldn't find the car.
A
شنو؟ انسرقت؟ في المولات يصير جذي
shinu? insirgat? fi l-mōlāt yṣīr chidhi
What? Had it been stolen? That happens in malls.
B
طول بالك، خلني أكمل!
ṭawwil bālak, khallni akammil!
Hang on, let me finish!
A
زين زين، كمل
zēn zēn, kammil
OK, OK, go on.
B
أمي قالت الطابق الثاني، وأبوي قال الثالث
ummi gālat iṭ-ṭābig ith-thāni, w ubūy gāl ith-thālith
My mum said the second floor, and my dad said the third.
A
وانت؟ ما تذكر وين خليتها؟
w inta? ma tidhkir wēn khallēt-ha?
And you? Don't you remember where you left it?
B
لا تقاطعني يا فهد! وين وصلت؟
la tgāṭiʿni yā Fahad! wēn wiṣalt?
Don't interrupt me, Fahad! Where was I?
A
أبوك قال الثالث
ubūk gāl ith-thālith
Your dad said the third.
B
هيه. المختصر، دورنا ساعة كاملة، وطلعت في الطابق الأول!
hē. il-mukhtaṣar, dawwarna sāʿa kāmla, w ṭilʿat fi ṭ-ṭābig il-awwal!
Right. Long story short, we searched for a whole hour, and it turned out to be on the first floor!
A
والله؟ وعلى فكرة، أنا بعد صار لي نفس الشي في المطار
wallāh? w ʿala fikra, ana baʿad ṣār-li nafs ish-shay fi l-maṭār
Seriously? And by the way, the same thing happened to me at the airport.
items: that happens, things like that happen (Kuwait)
hang on, be patient (to a man)
where was I? (lit. where did I get to?)
my mum, my dad and I (lit. I and my mum and my dad)

title: Checkpoint 4.6: karak at the camp
goal: Checkpoint: at a winter desert camp, tell Sēf about your new routine, make the karak while you explain each step, and laugh at your gym story
tip: Review, and now you say it: ṣār-li + time, ma ʿidt ākil, khaffaft, thalāth marrāt fi l-usbūʿ, khallah yighli, lēn yifūr, la tdhakkirni, jismi killah yʿawwirni. Give the steps in order: awwal shay, baʿdēn, lēn. Tease a friend who's up early: shu han-nashāṭ?
grammar: checkpoint 4.6 (s4u071–s4u082): routines, steps in order, narrative markers
dialogue: A
يا سالم، شو هالنشاط؟ الكل نايم، وانت صاحي من الفجر!
yā Sālim, shu han-nashāṭ? il-kill nāyim, w inta ṣāḥi min il-fajr!
Sālim, what's all this energy? Everyone's asleep, and you've been up since dawn!
B
صار لي شهر أنام بدري، والتلفون برا الخيمة
ṣār-li shahar anām badri, w it-tilifōn barra l-khēma
For a month now I've been going to bed early, with my phone outside the tent.
A
ما شاء الله! وبعدك تروح النادي؟
mā shāʼ allāh! w baʿdak trūḥ in-nādi?
Good for you! And are you still going to the gym?
B
هيه، ثلاث مرات في الأسبوع. وخففت الحلويات
hē, thalāth marrāt fi l-usbūʿ. w khaffaft il-ḥalawiyyāt
Yes, three times a week. And I've cut down on sweets.
A
زين، عيل انت بتسوي لنا الكرك. فهد يبي يتعلم
zēn, ʿayal inta bitsawwī-lna l-karak. Fahad yabi yitʿallam
Great, then you're making us the karak. Fahad wants to learn.
B
أبشر! أول شي الماي والشاي والهيل، وخله يغلي
abshir! awwal shay il-māy w ich-chāy w il-hēl, w khallah yighli
Right away! First the water, the tea and the cardamom, and let it boil.
A
والسكر؟ فهد يحبه حلو وايد
w is-sukkar? Fahad yḥibbah ḥilu wāyid
And the sugar? Fahad likes it really sweet.
B
بعدين الحليب والسكر، لين يفور مرتين
baʿdēn il-ḥalīb w is-sukkar, lēn yifūr marratēn
Then the milk and sugar, until it froths up twice.
A
ذكرتني بسالفتك في النادي، أول أسبوع!
dhakkartni b-sālftak fi n-nādi, awwal usbūʿ!
You've reminded me of your story at the gym, that first week!
B
لا تذكرني! جسمي كله كان يعورني
la tdhakkirni! jismi killah kān yʿawwirni
Don't remind me! My whole body ached.
items: what's all this energy? (teasing someone up early or very busy)
he likes it really sweet (a masculine thing: tea, coffee)
you've reminded me of your story (to a man)
